title: Optimizely Web Experimentation signup-flow flaw abused to inject skimmer, wallet swapper and iOS exploit kits into 178 organizations' scripts (OPTIMJACK)
why: Optimizely confirmed an attacker exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation account signup flow to write malicious JavaScript into customer projects; Report URI (Scott Helme) found 188 infected snippets for 178 organizations on Nov 16 (Zoom, BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, HSBC and others), confirmed by BleepingComputer and The Hacker News. It is a hosted-service flaw with no CVE, so it cannot be in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft advisory or Defender guidance for it. Nov 17: Optimizely's status notice confirms an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation and says it is fixed. Hudson Rock and researcher Kirk of Ohey traced the same loader in Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and minute-ly responses as early as Nov 13 (Help Net Security, infostealers.com). Still no CVE, and nothing from Microsoft. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV.
action: If you use Optimizely Web, review every project's Project JavaScript and experiment custom code for script you did not write (Report URI's checklist), rotate Optimizely users/API tokens, treat card data and non-HttpOnly cookies from Nov 16 pages as exposed, and push iOS/iPadOS to 18.7.3+ or 26.3+.
product: Optimizely Web Experimentation (hosted snippet / Project JavaScript); downstream iOS/iPadOS older than 18.7.3 / 26.3 targeted by the delivered kits

title: Apache Roller XML-RPC pre-auth Java deserialization RCE (4.0.0-6.1.4), Apache says actively exploited
why: Apache's Nov 17 advisory for CVE-2026-129448 says the flaw 'is being actively exploited'. It widens the September CVE-2026-82384 (6.1.5 only) back to 4.0.0, so scanners keyed on the old record miss older installs. Public PoCs for 82384 exist on GitHub and Sploitus. SecurityOnline reports it is not in CISA KEV, and CISA's last KEV additions were on Nov 13. Microsoft has published nothing on it.
action: Upgrade Roller to 6.1.6 or later. Until then, set enabledForExtensions=false in WEB-INF/web.xml or remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc servlet mapping and restart, then check that host for unexpected JVM child processes.

title: ScreenConnect RMM+ extension default/blank API secret (CVE-2026-127063) abused to push rogue clients and SCKit to managed endpoints
why: No longer ahead of Microsoft: Microsoft Security published 'SCKit abuses ScreenConnect' on Nov 13 with Defender hunting guidance, so Microsoft is tracking the campaign. ConnectWise marked its investigation complete on Nov 16 (20:00 UTC) and says partner action is still required; there is still no fixed RMM+ release and CVE-2026-127063 is not in CISA KEV.
action: On on-prem ScreenConnect, disable and uninstall RMM+ and related extensions now. Review Run Command and Toolbox history since Nov 11 for mass commands or ScreenConnect installer downloads. Make sure technician clients are on 26.6.5 or later.
product: DataComm RMM+ third-party extension for ConnectWise ScreenConnect (Huntress: 1.0.31 and 1.0.32 accept a blank key); no fixed version announced

title: wfx-loot: 4,837 hijacked GitHub accounts push a CI secret stealer; secrets taken from 1,800+ repos, with AWS and Entra ID persistence
why: Aikido, OX Security, SafeDep and StepSecurity report a live campaign since Nov 10: stolen tokens for 4,837 GitHub accounts opened ~62-66k probe PRs and the stealer ran in at least 1,806 repositories, still ongoing on Nov 12 with exfil moved to Telegram. The payload adds wfx-ci-* federated credentials to Entra ID apps and rewrites AWS role trust policies, which survive secret rotation. There is no CVE (no product bug), so no CISA KEV entry, and no Microsoft or GitHub guidance appeared in the sources reviewed. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV.
action: Search your GitHub org for PRs titled "docs: dependency audit notes" or wfx-docs branches since Nov 10; for any hit revoke that account's tokens and rotate every secret its workflows could reach, then hunt Entra ID for federated credentials named wfx-ci-* and AWS sessions named wfx-*.
vendor: GitHub (abuse of stolen developer tokens; no product flaw)
product: GitHub Actions workflows and npm postinstall hooks in any repository a compromised account can write to (since Nov 10, 2026)

title: WP Duplicate (LocalSync) WordPress plugin <=1.1.11: unauthenticated file upload to RCE, exploited, no patch
why: WPScan, the CNA, says the flaw is being actively exploited in the wild. A public exploit (Duplicate2Shell) was indexed on Sploitus and Vulners on Nov 15, and SecurityOnline reports that no patch exists. Microsoft has no advisory, and the flaw is not in CISA KEV, whose last additions were on Nov 13. WPScan has not published attack volumes or IOCs.
action: Deactivate and delete WP Duplicate from every WordPress site. Then look in wp-content/uploads and the plugin directories for PHP files you did not put there, and rotate admin credentials if you find any.
product: WP Duplicate WordPress plugin through 1.1.11 (no fixed release)

title: PostgreSQL CVE-2026-6460 type confusion: low-privileged database user to OS code execution, RCE technique now public
why: Researcher Mehmet Ince published a write-up turning the 22-year-old type confusion into code execution, and an independent researcher reproduced the crash with four SQL statements as a zero-privilege role (dev.to); the item hit Hacker News today. OffSeq and SecurityOnline report no exploitation, and it is not in CISA KEV. Hosted PostgreSQL services may be exposed, but no cloud-provider statement was found. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade to PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 or 14.25 (14 is now end-of-life), prioritising multi-tenant servers, and until then remove CREATE privileges from untrusted roles.
product: PostgreSQL before 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 and 14.25 (part of a 52-CVE release on Nov 12, 2026)

title: GeoVision GV-VMS 17.4.8.0 hosts exploited to deploy XMRig at 13 organizations (likely known unauthenticated WebCam Server RCE)
why: Huntress SOC saw attackers abuse internet-exposed GeoVision GV-VMS at 13 organizations (most activity Nov 8-10): commands spawned by GeoStartupAgentService.exe as SYSTEM, a BYOVD driver and IFEO hijacks to disable Microsoft Defender, then a DHT/PKARR Go loader and XMRig. Huntress told Help Net Security (Nov 16) that the sampled hosts ran GV-VMS 17.4.8.0 and that one of three unauthenticated RCEs in GeoVision's April 2026 advisory is the most likely entry point, but the exact CVE is not confirmed. No CVE for this activity is in CISA KEV and there is no Microsoft guidance; the campaign actively tries to switch Defender off. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade GV-VMS to V17.4.8.58 or later, take GeoVision management interfaces off the internet (VPN/IP allowlist), and hunt for cmd/PowerShell children of GeoStartupAgentService.exe and IFEO Debugger keys on Defender processes.

title: Apache Shiro DefaultLdapRealm accepts any password when authentication caching is enabled (CVE-2026-129349)
why: Apache disclosed it on oss-security on Nov 13 (CVSS 4.0 9.1, network, no privileges). It is a Java library, not a Microsoft product, and it is not in CISA KEV. No public PoC or exploitation reported. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV.
action: Find Java apps that bundle shiro-core with an LDAP realm and upgrade them to 3.0.2. Until then, turn off authentication caching on those realms.

title: Apache APISIX 3.20.0 fixes 7 flaws, incl. unauthenticated route-auth bypass (CVE-2026-124680) and identity-header spoofing (CVE-2026-124679)
why: Apache posted seven APISIX advisories on oss-security on Nov 13. Two let unauthenticated clients get past authentication in certain configurations. Not a Microsoft product, not in CISA KEV, and no public PoC or exploitation reported. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade APISIX gateways to 3.20.0. Until then, check for routes without auth that share an upstream with protected routes, and turn off forward-auth allow_degradation.

title: Cyrus SASL SRP mechanism authentication bypass: A=N forces zero shared secret (CVE-2026-129483)
why: VulnCheck (CNA) published it Nov 15 with an upstream fix commit and oss-security post; CVSS 9.1/9.3, network, no privileges. No exploitation reported and not in CISA KEV. Only servers that enable the SRP SASL mechanism are exposed. A Microsoft CSAF/VEX record exists for the package, but no Microsoft product guidance. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV.
action: Check whether any service offers the SRP SASL mechanism (mech_list / installed libsrp plugin) and disable or remove the SRP plugin until distro packages carry upstream commit fb3724f.

title: Arize Phoenix unauthenticated applyChatTemplate format-string flaw leaks PHOENIX_SECRET, enabling admin session forgery (CVSS 10.0)
why: GitHub advisory GHSA-gfv3-m769-5xm3 and the CVE record (published Nov 16) describe an endpoint that is unauthenticated on default installs and exposes PHOENIX_SECRET, allowing admin session-token forgery. No public exploit or in-the-wild use reported; not in CISA KEV, no Microsoft coverage. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade Phoenix to 15.7.0 or later, keep it off the public internet, and rotate PHOENIX_SECRET and any credentials in its environment if it was exposed.
product: Phoenix AI observability platform 13.0.0 to before 15.7.0

title: NoisyTCP: Linux kernel TCP pre-auth remote crash (CVE-2026-99288), present since 4.4, full details public after embargo
why: Hyunwoo Kim posted the full NoisyTCP write-up to oss-security on Nov 15 once the linux-distros embargo ended. A remote attacker with no login can panic any Linux host that has a TCP listener and spreads packets over 2+ RX queues or RPS (default on most cloud VMs). Kim has a private lab PoC (5 s to 2 min against KVM guests), but no exploit code is public and nobody has reported attacks. Debian and Oracle UEK have fixed kernels. As of Nov 15-16, Ubuntu and RHEL/Rocky/Alma had no fix yet. It is not in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft/MSRC (Azure Linux) entry in the collected data. Scored low because the impact is DoS only: Red Hat 7.5, no NVD score. Nov 16 update: BleepingComputer and others now cover it; Debian and Arch ship fixed kernels, Ubuntu and RHEL trackers still list it as unfixed/affected; researcher has still not published exploit code and no attacks are reported. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV.
action: Patch internet-facing Linux hosts to a kernel with commit 4e2b3ef19e0e (6.12.117/6.18.63/7.3.4 or your distro backport) and reboot. Until a distro fix ships, Ubuntu/RHEL hosts can set net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies=0 in every netns, or use a single RX queue with RPS/RFS off. Weigh the SYN-flood trade-off first.
product: Linux kernel 4.4 through 6.12.116, 6.13-6.18.62, 6.19-7.3.3 (TCP established-socket lookup); EOL 7.2 gets no fix

title: 'Hello Again': fTPM lockout rollback via RPMC flaws lets attackers with physical access brute-force Windows Hello and BitLocker TPM+PIN
why: Academic paper (arXiv 2611.18126, CCS '26, Nov 13) demonstrates end-to-end on locked hardware: a 4-digit Hello PIN in 40 hours, BitLocker 6-digit TPM+PIN worst case 20 days, by rolling back fTPM anti-hammering state (Winbond RPMC HMAC key leak via glitching; AMD controller not verifying increments; some AMD boards with no rollback protection). Per the authors, no vendor committed to a root-cause fix; Microsoft only raised its recommended minimum Hello PIN to 6 digits. No CVE, no MSRC advisory. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV.
action: For lost/stolen-device risk, enforce Windows Hello and BitLocker pre-boot PINs of at least 6 (preferably 8+) digits or alphanumeric PINs via policy.
product: Windows Hello and BitLocker TPM+PIN on x86 systems using firmware TPMs (AMD, Intel, Pluton) backed by SPI flash

title: Copeland/Dixell XWEB EVO (EOL) batch: pre-auth root command injection and hardcoded backdoor password (CVE-2026-124002..124015)
why: VulnCheck published a batch of 14 XWEB EVO CVEs on Nov 12, including unauthenticated root command injection (CVSS 9.8) and a hardcoded admin backdoor password. This comes while the sibling XWEB PRO (CVE-2026-25085) is being exploited in refrigeration sabotage. There is no public exploit and no reported in-the-wild use, and none of the CVEs is in CISA KEV. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV.
action: Take XWEB EVO web interfaces off the internet now, put them behind VPN or allowlists, and plan to replace these end-of-service units.
product: XWEB EVO refrigeration/HVAC supervisor, 4.3.0 through 5.8.8 depending on CVE; product line end of service March 2026

title: Dassault 3DEXPERIENCE Station Launcher App: unauthenticated deserialization RCE (CVSS 10.0) plus two command injections
why: Vendor (3DS CNA) advisories published Nov 16: CVE-2026-93664 unauthenticated deserialization RCE (CVSS 10.0) and CVE-2026-77033/19732 OS command injection. No public exploit or exploitation reported; not in CISA KEV. Rechecked Nov 17 17Z: CISA's last KEV additions were Nov 13 (none since); still not in KEV.
action: Apply the fix packs named in the 3DS advisories for CVE-2026-93664/77033/19732 and restrict network access to Station Launcher services.
product: 3DEXPERIENCE platform Station Launcher App, R2023x through R2026x
